title: Go SDK: sliding-window grace period + request-priority adapter for streaming cancellation ergonomics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a Go SDK streaming adapter that introduces a configurable sliding-buffer grace period and request-priority hints to improve cancellation ergonomics and fairness. Goal: give callers a simple API to request an ordered, best-effort flush window after cancel/timeout, while preventing head-of-line starvation for high-priority streams and reducing spurious restarts and retries. This work covers API ergonomics, runtime manager changes, telemetry, and tests.
acceptance_criteria: New API: StreamWithGrace(ctx, opts...) that accepts GracePeriod and Priority hints and is documented in SDK README.
Adapter integrates with existing stream session manager without breaking current cancellation semantics for callers that don't opt-in.
Unit and integration tests cover: normal cancellation, context deadline exceed, early client cancel with remaining tokens flush, priority preemption behavior, and interaction with server-side aborts.
Benchmarks show <=5% p50 token latency regression and measurable reduction in reconnects for typical chat workload (10k sample trace).
Telemetry emitted: grace_window_start/grace_window_end, grace_consumed_count, priority_preemptions, flush_success/failure, and reconnects avoided metric.
implementation_notes: Add stream adapter layer in internal/streaming/adapter.go exposing StreamWithGrace and StreamPriority enums.
Change stream session manager to support per-stream soft-fail windows: when ctx cancelled, mark stream as 'grace' for configured duration and allow partial KV cache eviction behavior to be delayed.
Implement a fair scheduler that uses Priority hint + remaining grace time to decide token dispatch order across concurrent streams on a connection.
Do not change wire protocol; implement all behavior client-side to preserve compatibility with hosted and dedicated backends.
Expose telemetry hooks via existing opentelemetry tracing spans and add metrics to Console dashboards (metric names above).
Add examples in examples/go/streaming/grace_period_example.go and small code snippet in README showing defer cancel and handling of streamed final events.
API should be opt-in; default behavior remains current immediate-cancel semantics to avoid regressions for existing apps.
test_plan: Unit tests for adapter methods: grace window arithmetic, priority comparator, scheduler fairness under synthetic load.
Integration test: end-to-end local emulation with fake server that simulates in-flight token emission, client cancels after N tokens and asserts flush behavior.
Chaos test: kill connection mid-grace and assert reconnect + resume semantics stay within existing guarantees.
Performance benchmark: compare p50/p95/p99 token latency and connect counts with and without grace adapter across 1000 simulated streams.
Manual QA: validate example app in macOS dev env and Linux CI container; review telemetry in staging Console.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Asha Patel: Triage note. Spike shows a 12% reduction in reconnects when allowing a 150ms flush window for chat workloads. Moving to In Progress. Assigned to Marcos.

2026-03-03 - Marcos Alvarez: Drafted API surface. Initial prototype implemented in internal branch: feat/grace-adapter. Pushed small benchmark harness to github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/tree/feat/grace-adapter/bench.

2026-03-05 - Design review (Liam Chen): Concern about head-of-line blocking when many low-priority clients opt into long grace windows. Suggested adding max_concurrent_grace_per_connection and absolute timeout cap. Marked as must-have.

2026-03-06 - Marcos Alvarez: Implemented max_concurrent_grace_per_connection and global cap. Also added scheduler that prefers streams with higher priority and shorter remaining grace. Benchmarks re-run: reconnect reduction down to 8% (was 12%) but head-of-line stalls resolved.
2026-03-08 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/492. Requesting review from runtime team (Nadia, Omar). Added README snippet and example app.

2026-03-09 - Nadia Park (runtime): Noted potential race when a stream enters grace and session is recycled. Suggested a small refactor of session lifecycle to mark grace streams pinned to connection until grace expires or flush completes. Created subtask: ENG-518211.

2026-03-10 - Marcos Alvarez: Refactored session lifecycle per Nadia's feedback. Updated tests to cover pinned-grace semantics. Running CI. Next: address performance profiling feedback and add telemetry tags for customer_id and model_id to console metrics.
